newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates rise as reserves dip.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates rise as reserves dip.

text.p: German call money rates nudged slightly higher on Friday amid pre-weekend shifts after reserve holdings fell, but dealers said there was no reason to fear that rates would march steadily higher next week.
The bulk of trades was conducted around 3.10 percent on Friday after rates traded between 3.05/3.10 percent on Thursday.

Dealers said liquidity conditions, which had been mostly ample during the earlier part of the week, tightened slightly on Friday. Tighter conditions were also reflected in daily reserve holdings, which dipped on Thursday.

Dealers however said they were slightly puzzled by the drop off in reserves saying they had no ready explanation for it. But they cautioned conditions did not yet constitute any sort of liquidity squeeze.

For Thursday banks held 37.5 billion marks at the Bundesbank, down from 39.4 billion marks one day earlier. The monthly average holdings also dipped to 41.9 billion marks from 42.8 billion marks. Lombard borrowings however were negligible.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.13700 percent on Friday after 3.10567 percent on Thursday. --Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
